audit.why: 50.14% over 363 games — an even lane that Fiora front-loads and Warwick reclaims with sustain. 6/10 is right.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl (E) is never mentioned anywhere on the page, and no cooldown numbers appear.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Warwick gains damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to flee for 1 second.' It is 15/14/13/12/11s. A 1s flee breaks your Bladework sequence and the damage reduction eats the Vital burst — it is the second spell you must respect after the suppress. Infinite Duress is 110/90/70s and suppresses for 1.5s.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl added to whys[3], dontsFull[1].d and breakdown.cooldowns with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] is titled 'Anti-heal his Q sustain' but its body was generic trade text.
audit.why: Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on the target's maximum health and heals for damage dealt, on 8s falling to 6s — that is what anti-heal is buying against.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d now names the spell and the item.

edits.after: His Q heal, below-50% passive and a 15s Primal Howl (2.5s damage reduction into a 1s fear) come online — early anti-heal keeps it a coinflip.

edits.before: Warwick wastes Infinite Duress — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Jaws of the Beast heals off max-HP damage — Executioner's Calling early.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Primal Howl fears you for 1s and cuts his damage taken — bait it out.

edits.before: - Warwick Infinite Duress: matchup-defining — His all-in lock. Riposte it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Warwick Infinite Duress: 110s at rank 1, 70s at rank 3 — a 1.5s suppress. Riposte the leap. - Primal Howl: 15s at rank 1 — damage reduction, then a 1s fear. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

notes: Riot's own text tags Infinite Duress as a channel ('interruptible — any CC cancels it' in the derived flags). Whether Fiora's Riposte stun can break an already-applied suppress is not answerable from the kit files, so I left the existing 'parry the leap, return a stun' framing exactly as written rather than extending it. spikes[2]/whys[5] name Profane Hydra while report[8] names Ravenous Hydra — the recurring Fiora build inconsistency, untouched.
